questions.question: What is ERB and how do you write it in Rails views?
questions.title: ERB Basics
questions.direct_answer: ERB (Embedded Ruby) is Rails' default templating language: it's HTML with Ruby sprinkled in using tags. <% ... %> runs Ruby (no output): <% @posts.each do |p| %>. <%= ... %> runs Ruby AND outputs the result: <%= @post.title %>. <% end %> closes a block. You use it to loop and display data: iterate with @posts.each, output with <%= p.title %>, interpolate with #{...} inside strings. Escape HTML by default (<%= %> escapes; use raw or html_safe to skip — only for trusted content). Keep views dumb: just show @vars the controller set; no business logic in the view.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know <% %> (run, no output) vs <%= %> (run and output), and that <%= %> escapes HTML by default.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using <% %> where you need output (nothing shows), or raw on untrusted content (XSS risk).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: ERB is HTML with Ruby: <% %> runs (no output), <%= %> runs + outputs (escapes HTML by default). Loop with each, output with <%=. Keep views dumb.
